# Replay fixtures (T-032)

**Synthetic speech, not a human voice.** Nothing here was recorded from a
microphone. The `replay-*.wav` files are generated by
[`../gen_replay_fixtures.py`](../gen_replay_fixtures.py): Piper
(`desktop/tts/piper.exe`, voice `en_US-amy-medium`, noise_scale and noise_w 0 so
the text gives the same samples every run) joined with digitally generated
silence and seeded low-level noise, resampled to 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM.

They exist for exact, repeatable timing in headless tests (`CC_REPLAY_WAV`):
a 0.9 s pause is 0.9 s every run. They say nothing about how a real person
pauses; whether a replay counts as evidence in a person's own voice is the
owner's call (T-019 AC-7/AC-8, decision D-8).

Regenerate: `python desktop/tests/gen_replay_fixtures.py`. Check that a rerun is
byte-identical: `python desktop/tests/gen_replay_fixtures.py --check`.

| File | Content | Used for |
|------|---------|----------|
| `replay-a-mid-pause.wav` | "Show me the open tickets" / 0.9 s pause / "and which ones are blocked" | AC-1, 2, 5 |
| `replay-b-gap-3s.wav` | "Show me the open tickets." / 3 s gap / "Which ones are blocked?" | AC-3 |
| `replay-c-five-pauses.wav` | one sentence in six pieces with five 0.9 s pauses | AC-4 |
| `replay-d-silence.wav` | 3 s digital silence | AC-11 |
| `replay-e-low-noise.wav` | 3 s steady noise, about -40 dBFS, no speech | AC-11 |
| `replay-f-clicks-in-window.wav` | "Show me the open tickets", then three 3 ms clicks 0.25 s apart | AC-6 |
| `replay-g-silence-hallucination.wav` | 10 s digital silence | AC-11 (a transcript that is a list entry) |
| `replay-g2-noise-sound-tag.wav` | 8 s steady noise | AC-10/11 (a transcript that is a sound tag) |

Every spoken file has 0.5 s of faint seeded noise before and after, so the
endpointer calibrates on a room rather than on digital zero. (f) is a sentence
plus clicks, not clicks alone: AC-6 is about clicks inside the merge window
that FOLLOWS speech.

## What the real engine heard (hallucination search, FR-6 g)

`desktop/stt/whisper-cli.exe -m desktop/stt/ggml-base.en.bin -f <file> -nt -np`
(base.en, whisper.cpp CLI, run on 2026-10-06; the shipped whisper-server may
differ slightly):

| Input | Transcript |
|-------|-----------|
| `replay-a-mid-pause.wav` | "Show me the open tickets and which ones are blocked." |
| `replay-b-gap-3s.wav` | "Show me the open tickets. Which ones are blocked?" |
| `replay-c-five-pauses.wav` | "Show me the open tickets that are blocked or waiting on someone right now" |
| `replay-f-clicks-in-window.wav` | "Show me the open tickets." |
| `replay-d-silence.wav`, `replay-g-silence-hallucination.wav` | "you" |
| `replay-e-low-noise.wav` | "(machinery whirring)" |
| `replay-g2-noise-sound-tag.wav` | "(clippers whirring)" |

The search tried digital silence (10 s, 30 s), white noise at four levels,
50 Hz and 120 Hz hum, pink-ish noise, keyboard-like clicks and shaped
"breath" noise. Silence gave "you" (an entry in the FR-15 list); every noise
gave a parenthesised sound tag (what FR-15 strips). No "Thank you." was found
in the time spent.
